weapons.name: Unarmed Strike
weapons.notes: The book prints damage and traits as 'Varies; typically ...'; these are the typical values.

armor.name: Padded Hood
armor.description: Layers of quilted cloth protecting the head and neck. Light, quiet, and comfortable, but intended to soften blows rather than stop powerful weapons outright.

armor.name: Leather Helm
armor.description: Thick leather shaped and hardened around the skull while leaving the face and ears open. It provides unobtrusive protection without metal weight or noise.

armor.name: Mail Hood
armor.description: Interlocking metal rings covering the head, neck, and shoulders. Its broad, flexible coverage resists cuts well, but adds weight and does little to stop the force of a heavy blow.

armor.name: Skullcap
armor.description: A close-fitting steel cap protecting the crown and sides of the skull while leaving the face and neck exposed. It can be hidden beneath a hood or large hat.

armor.name: War Hat
armor.description: A steel helmet with a broad, sloping brim that shelters the head from descending blows, missiles, and falling debris. The open face preserves awareness and breathing.

armor.name: Open Helm
armor.description: A fitted steel helmet protecting the skull, temples, cheeks, and nape while leaving the face open. It offers strong all-purpose protection without substantially restricting sight or breathing.

armor.name: Full Helm
armor.description: An enclosing steel helmet with movable face protection. Lowering the visor gives excellent head and facial protection at the cost of peripheral awareness; raising it restores an open view.

armor.name: Light Gambeson
armor.description: A lightly quilted coat protecting the torso and hips without burdening movement. It may be worn alone or serve as the foundation beneath other armor.

armor.name: Heavy Gambeson
armor.description: A thick, densely layered quilted coat designed to absorb impact as armor in its own right. It remains quiet and comfortable but is hotter and bulkier than a light gambeson.

armor.name: Leather Cuirass
armor.description: Thick, shaped, and hardened leather protecting the chest, back, and abdomen. “Leather” here means armor-grade hardened hide: not ordinary clothing leather.

armor.name: Mail Shirt
armor.description: Interlocking metal rings protecting the torso, shoulders, and upper arms. It moves naturally with the body and resists cuts exceptionally well, but requires padding and remains vulnerable to purpose-made narrow points.

armor.name: Lamellar Armor
armor.description: Overlapping rows of small rigid plates laced together around the torso. Lamellar needs no supporting fabric for its structure.

armor.name: Brigandine
armor.description: Overlapping steel plates riveted inside a fitted cloth or leather garment. It combines strong protection with more give and less exposed metal than a plate cuirass.

armor.name: Plate Cuirass
armor.description: Shaped steel plates protecting the chest, back, abdomen, and often the hips. Its rigid surfaces deflect and distribute blows extremely well, but the cuirass works best when fitted to its wearer.

armor.name: Padded Sleeves
armor.description: Quilted cloth protecting the shoulders, arms, and elbows. They remain light and flexible enough for climbing, archery, weapon work, or spellcasting.

armor.name: Leather Armguards
armor.description: Shaped leather defenses covering the exposed portions of the upper arms, elbows, and forearms while leaving the hands free. Gaps preserve mobility but remain vulnerable to precise attacks.

armor.name: Mail Sleeves
armor.description: Interlocking rings protecting the arms through their full range of motion. They resist cuts without rigid joints, but their weight is noticeable during prolonged weapon use.

armor.name: Splinted Arms
armor.description: Narrow metal strips fixed to a leather or textile backing over the upper arms and forearms, with joint protection at the elbows. They are affordable and field-repairable but leave more gaps than complete plate.

armor.name: Plate Armguards
armor.description: Articulated steel protecting the shoulders, elbows, and forearms while leaving selected inner surfaces or the hands less enclosed. They give efficient protection without the full Load of complete arm harness.

armor.name: Plate Arms
armor.description: Articulated steel plates protecting the shoulders, upper arms, elbows, forearms, and hands.

armor.name: Padded Leggings
armor.description: Quilted cloth protecting the thighs, knees, and lower legs. They permit unrestricted movement and may serve as the foundation beneath heavier leg armor.

armor.name: Leather Legguards
armor.description: Hardened leather covering the exposed fronts and sides of the thighs, knees, and shins. They are quiet and light, but their straps and gaps leave openings for precise attacks.

armor.name: Mail Leggings
armor.description: Interlocking rings providing broad protection from thigh to lower leg. They are flexible, but weight carried on the legs is particularly tiring during running and climbing.

armor.name: Splinted Legguards
armor.description: Metal strips secured to padded or leather supports over the thighs and shins, with separate knee protection. They provide efficient partial armor that can be repaired without an armorer’s forge.

armor.name: Lamellar Legguards
armor.description: Small overlapping plates laced into panels protecting the thighs and other exposed portions of the legs. They provide broad, repairable protection but are bulkier than partial plate.

armor.name: Plate Legguards
armor.description: Fitted steel plates protecting the knees, shins, and exposed portions of the thighs while omitting some enclosing plates. They retain most of plate’s defensive value at reduced Load.

armor.name: Plate Legs
armor.description: Articulated steel plates protecting the thighs, knees, and lower legs. The components are fitted and joined so the legs can bend and move while remaining substantially enclosed.

shields.name: Tower Shield
shields.note: No Gear bonus to Guard. Gives you Cover when Raised, and Greater Cover if you Take Cover while it is Raised.
